name: Damion Shelton
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman of the Board, Agility (Agility Robotics); AVP & Executive Director, Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, Carnegie Mellon University
profile: Carnegie Mellon robotics PhD who co-founded Agility Robotics in 2015 as a spinout of Jonathan Hurst's OSU legged-locomotion lab and served as CEO until 2024 (Peggy Johnson succeeded him; he then served as president). He now chairs Agility's board and runs CMU's Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, mentoring founders.
interesting_fact: His founder advice: 'build something that's useful to someone rapidly, as opposed to having it be an indefinite science project' - the approach he used to take Agility from research robots to warehouse humanoids.
deep_cut_fact: Before Agility he co-founded threeRivers 3D, where as CTO he designed a low-cost, high-volume laser scanner for novice users in healthcare; he describes himself as a 'jack-of-all-trades roboticist' who left academia to build products.
notes: Now based at CMU (Pittsburgh); CMU Swartz Center may be a better route than Agility. Has written for TechCrunch (author page exists) and spoken at TC Disrupt. Exact end dates of CEO/president roles vary across sources.

name: Steven Hunter
profile: British former leveraged-finance professional (J.P. Morgan LevFin in London; investment executive at Babson Capital covering European high yield and leveraged loans) who co-founded 9fin in 2016 with Huss El-Sheikh. 9fin is an AI-native data, news and analytics platform for debt capital markets used by 350+ institutions; it has raised 250M+ USD and was valued around 1.3B USD at its Series C.
interesting_fact: 9fin has become a go-to voice on financing of the AI/data-center buildout (e.g. neocloud and CoreWeave debt); Hunter discussed 'Who's funding the AI buildout?' on Bloomberg Radio in Sept 2026 - directly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer, graduating from the University of Bristol with a first-class honours law degree; his co-founder Huss El-Sheikh is also a Bristol graduate (MEng aerospace engineering).
notes: Media-friendly (Bloomberg Radio, NYSE Wired). team@9fin.com is a general company inbox linked in the site header. Some profiles mention Credit Suisse in his history; the official bio lists only J.P. Morgan and Babson.

name: Chris Shaw
profile: UWA electrical-engineering graduate who co-founded Advanced Navigation with Xavier Orr in 2012, building the hardware for its AI-based inertial navigation systems. The ~1B USD-valued firm supplies navigation for drones, ships, defence vehicles, satellites and a NASA CLPS lunar lander, with customers in 70+ countries. He became sole CEO after Orr stepped back in 2024.
interesting_fact: Advanced Navigation's Botany (Sydney) factory is one of only four facilities in the world able to make strategic-grade fibre-optic gyroscopes; Shaw argues 'it's a myth that Australia is slow and uncompetitive' in manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days Shaw assembled every unit himself in his Subiaco (Perth) garage, and while still in the garage he built the company's first assembly robot to boost production; the pair sold hundreds of units in year one and were profitable within nine months.
notes: He and Orr both had side jobs at early WA drone companies before founding. Good energy/defence angle: offshore wind-farm inspection, GPS-denied navigation.
